title: An 81-day spot-area history improves daily radio fits but leaves a Cycle 25 excess in the tested windows
abstract: We test whether recent spot-area history explains the Cycle 25 radio excess. Daily models in cycle months 25 to 59 use current area, previous 81-day mean area and a future-area control. At fixed HMI area the radio offset falls from 8.34% to 7.64% after past history is added; the conditional 95% block interval is 3.53 to 13.34%. Ground area gives 12.36% after adjustment, with limits 9.22 to 15.99%. Paired contrasts do not show a clear special reduction from past rather than future area. A prediction test with held-out calendar blocks and 81-day gaps shows useful past information for ground area: log-radio RMSE falls from 0.09693 to 0.08870, while future area gives 0.09848. Daily memory information therefore does not remove the cycle offset in these models. Tests with other windows and block lengths give limits on this result. The models do not identify a solar cause, a decay time or instrument stability. Code, aggregate results, a figure, input hashes and retrieval instructions are included. External observations and daily derivatives remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Daily Cycle 25 radio offsets at fixed area and area history. Points and conditional 95% calendar-block intervals. Future area is a diagnostic reconstruction.
